name: Hazzard
caption: Held the IPW-XFWL E-Championship through the fall of 2003 before losing it in a three-way Triangle Turbulence match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Frenzy
caption: A midcard wrestler who competed in the Number One Contender's Jumble Match and later in the North Pole Street Fight as part of PRIDE.

name: Bouncer
caption: A former IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Champion who won the E-Championship from Hazzard at Hardcore Holiday in a three-way Triangle Turbulence match.

name: Mark Prohibition
caption: Won the IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Championship from Bouncer in mid-2003 and lost it to Venom in a two-out-of-three-falls match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Pawel Trojakow
caption: One half of The Russians, a tag team that challenged for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship in a chain match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Igor Maskarow
caption: One half of The Russians, a tag team that challenged for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship in a chain match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Homer D. Poe
caption: One half of a midcard tag team defeated by The Russians on Impact Xtreme.

name: Dirk Dean
caption: One half of a midcard tag team defeated by The Russians on Impact Xtreme.

name: Roadkill
caption: Billed as "the Enforcer" and "the Monster," fought in IPW-XFWL's hardcore matches through late 2003, including a three-way Triangle Turbulence match for the E-Championship at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Razor
caption: Billed as the original monster of IPW-XFWL and its first World Champion; fought Roadkill in a no-disqualification Battle Of The Monsters match on Impact Xtreme.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Chester McDoogle
caption: A self-declared "Heel Monster Killer" who brought Razor into IPW-XFWL to target Roadkill.

name: Killmore
caption: Wrestled under the nickname Cix; defeated Venom on Impact Xtreme and teamed with Rex and The Funk Master in the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Venom
caption: Lost to Killmore on Impact Xtreme, then won the IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Championship from Mark Prohibition in a two-out-of-three-falls match at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: D Money
caption: A wrestler whose ringside presence during Killmore's match with Venom on Impact Xtreme drew Venom's own accusation of interference.

name: Amanda Clark
caption: Won a six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme, then captured the IPW-XFWL Women's Championship from Peaches in a ladder match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Living Dead Girl
caption: Billed under her own name as Veronica; lost to Amanda Clark in the opening match of a six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Phoenix
caption: Lost to Amanda Clark in the second match of a six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme, then helped Psyklone defeat Spindle at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Peaches
caption: Won the final match of a six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme to become the number-one contender for the Women's Championship, then lost the title to Amanda Clark in a ladder match at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: The Hurrikat
caption: Attacked Peaches with a steel chair during the six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme, drawing a disqualification.

name: Shadow Seductress
caption: Lost to Peaches in the deciding match of a six-woman gauntlet series on Impact Xtreme.

name: Mistress Of Light
caption: The reigning IPW-XFWL Women's Champion as of late September 2003, described on-air as working with disadvantaged children abroad rather than defending the title that week.

name: Tyrant
caption: The IPW-XFWL World Champion through the fall of 2003, defeated by 411 in a triple-threat Bring Your Own Weapon match at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Kevin J. Ridge
caption: A member of the tag team The Future; lost a sixty-minute Iron Man match to Big Daddy Cool Dudley at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Lance
caption: A member of the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Champions The Future; his chain match against The Russians at Hardcore Holiday ended in a disputed double pinfall.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Paul
caption: A member of the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Champions The Future; his chain match against The Russians at Hardcore Holiday ended in a disputed double pinfall.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Big Daddy Cool Dudley
caption: Won a sixty-minute Iron Man match against Kevin J. Ridge at Hardcore Holiday, four falls to three.

name: Molly Ringwald's Boyfriend
caption: Big Daddy Cool Dudley's tag-team partner and comedic sidekick, appearing in backstage vignettes around Impact Xtreme and Hardcore Holiday.

name: Joey Gots
caption: IPW-XFWL's on-screen booking authority, who set the promotion's War Games match and oversaw Hardcore Holiday from his office.

name: Bob Munroe
caption: The on-screen agent of Ben "Lions" North, who picked one of the two ten-man War Games teams opposite Joey Gots on Impact Xtreme.

name: Spindle
caption: A self-described "living legend" of the old XFWL; lost the barbwire-and-weapons Nightmare Before Christmas match to Psyklone at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Rex
caption: Teamed with Killmore and The Funk Master to defeat PRIDE in the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: The Funk Master
caption: Also billed as Pimpslap; teamed with Killmore and Rex to defeat PRIDE in the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Yoshihiro Toyama
caption: A member of the stable PRIDE, defeated by Killmore, Rex, and The Funk Master in the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

name: J-Sleazy
caption: A member of the stable PRIDE, defeated by Killmore, Rex, and The Funk Master in the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

name: The Evil Elf
caption: A comedic interference character who bit two competitors during the North Pole Street Fight at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Scout
caption: An on-screen IPW-XFWL authority figure who confiscated the Tag Team Championship belts amid a disputed finish at Hardcore Holiday and later declared the title vacant pending a January tournament.

name: Hades McFan
caption: A backstage interviewer for IPW-XFWL, a holdover from the old XFWL broadcast team.

name: Psyklone
caption: Returned to IPW-XFWL after more than a year away and defeated Spindle in the barbwire-and-weapons Nightmare Before Christmas match at Hardcore Holiday, with Phoenix's help.

name: JuggaØ
caption: A former XFWL owner who spent the fall of 2003 wrestling in a mask as "Lions" before being unmasked at Funhouse; later challenged Tyrant for the IPW-XFWL World Championship in a triple-threat Bring Your Own Weapon match at Hardcore Holiday, ultimately losing the title bout to 411.
Billed as "the Big F'N Deal"; won the IPW-XFWL World Championship from Tyrant in a triple-threat Bring Your Own Weapon match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Max
caption: A former IPW-XFWL World Champion billed as "the Greatest Thing Since God"; lost a stretcher match to Caramel at Hardcore Holiday after a botched dive.

identity.note: Name shared with an unrelated wrestler of the same generic ring name at another promotion; no evidence links the two.

name: Caramel
caption: Billed as "Cap'in Nasty" and a member of the stable PRIDE; defeated Max in a stretcher match at Hardcore Holiday.

name: Bobby White
caption: Half of White Shadow, the tag team that came within a hair of taking the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship from The Future in a chain match at Hardcore Holiday.

tenures.note: Billed as "The Natural" Bobby White; teamed with Aaron Briggs as White Shadow across a title shot and two further matches against The Future and The Russians.

name: Aaron Briggs
caption: Half of White Shadow, the tag team that came within a hair of taking the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship from The Future in a chain match at Hardcore Holiday.

tenures.note: Billed as "The Shadow" Aaron Briggs; teamed with Bobby White as White Shadow across a title shot and two further matches against The Future and The Russians.

name: John Norvilas
caption: A former IPW-XFWL World Champion whose brief reign was reversed by Tyrant and Joey Gots six days after he won it; spent the fall of 2003 on an escalating campaign of violence against Tyrant that culminated in a Rage In The Cage title match at Funhouse.

tenures.note: Also billed as the Human Hemorrhoid; a ten-man War Games participant, and the losing challenger in Tyrant's Rage In The Cage title defense at Funhouse.

name: Everest
caption: A seven-foot, four-hundred-pound enforcer hired by Joey Gots to end 411's career; lost their first singles match at Funhouse despite the size mismatch.

tenures.note: Introduced as Joey Gots's hired gun against 411, debuting with a chokeslam through the ring at Fallout and wrestling him in a singles match at Funhouse.

name: Gotti
caption: Half of the tag team Gangsta Heaven, twice unsuccessful challengers for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship against The Future.

tenures.note: Teamed with Hoffa as Gangsta Heaven; lost a number-one contender's match to The Two Dudes.

name: Hoffa
caption: Half of the tag team Gangsta Heaven, twice unsuccessful challengers for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship against The Future.

tenures.note: Teamed with Gotti as Gangsta Heaven; lost a number-one contender's match to The Two Dudes.

name: Donny the Donkey
caption: A live-animal mascot who accompanies The Two Dudes to ringside.

tenures.note: Non-wrestling mascot for the tag team The Two Dudes (Big Daddy Cool Dudley and Molly Ringwald's Boyfriend).

name: The Incredible Edible Kid
caption: A jobber pinned by Spindle on Impact Xtreme, then rescued from a post-match chair beating by "Lions" Ben North.

tenures.note: Lost quickly to Spindle; the post-match beatdown he suffered set up Spindle's own feud with Lions.

name: Firestrike
caption: A debuting wrestler aligned with Razor and Chester McDoogle as the Heel Busters; challenged for the IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Championship in a four-way match at Funhouse.

tenures.note: Debuted against Frenzy, defeated J-Sleazy, and challenged Mark Prohibition for the Junior Heavyweight title in a four-way match at Funhouse.

name: Boom
caption: D Money's associate in the Money Clique; ejected from ringside for interfering in D Money's match against Killmore at Funhouse.

tenures.note: Accompanied D Money to the ring carrying a briefcase of cash; interfered in his match against Killmore at Funhouse before being sent backstage by the referee.

name: Dante
caption: A masked wrestling monk under a self-imposed vow of silence, teamed with Firestrike as the Heel Busters' own rival team took the fall.

tenures.note: Teamed with Firestrike against Frenzy and J-Sleazy on Impact Xtreme, 1 November 2003, pinning Frenzy with a shooting star press.

name: Akira
caption: A returning highflier, formerly of the tag team Asian Foundation with Everest; reunited with JuggaØ and a turned Everest as the stable Thryce.

tenures.note: Named as JuggaØ's chosen partner against Tyrant and Everest on 1 November 2003; wrestled the match on 8 November, watching as Everest turned on Tyrant to reveal the three of them as Thryce.

name: Big Van Driver
caption: A nearly-400-pound wrestler billed from Japan, hired by Amanda Clark as a soft first defense of her self-purchased "Real" Women's Championship; lost anyway.

tenures.note: Lost to Amanda Clark on Impact Xtreme, 8 November 2003, after Amanda struck her with a foreign object (a roll of coins).

name: Mr. Vernon
caption: A MegaCard Corporation representative who sponsored the promotion's own eight-man Combat match and personally invited the Two Dudes to compete in it.

tenures.note: Announced and sponsored the eight-man MegaCard Combat match on Impact Xtreme, 1 November 2003, offering the winning team a $20,000 prize.

name: Cousin Vinny
caption: Joey Gots' cousin, a recurring comic backstage presence who once dressed as a fast-counting fake referee at Spindle's request.

tenures.note: Delivered minor business news to Joey Gots backstage on 8 November 2003; dressed as a fake referee for Spindle's main event against JuggaØ on 15 November, fast-counting a near-fall before being ejected from the ring.

name: Heather Sever
caption: A debuting behemoth with an unsettling gimmick (self-inflicted chops, a blank stare), lost a non-title challenge to Peaches before falling to Phoenix a week later.

tenures.note: Debuted in a non-title loss to Women's Champion Peaches on 15 November 2003; lost again to Phoenix on 22 November.

name: Taurus
caption: A Junior Heavyweight hopeful wrestling thirty pounds over his own stated weight limit; lost his debut to Firestrike after re-injuring Chester McDoogle's neck.

tenures.note: Debuted against Firestrike on Impact Xtreme, 15 November 2003, losing after Chester McDoogle took a Gore meant for Firestrike.
